projects.name: Microstructure Discovery Factory
fullBullets: Designed and built a causal market-data capture, persistence, replay, research and validation system spanning Binance, OKX, Bybit, Deribit and Hyperliquid. The pipeline runs from WebSocket acquisition and normalization through exact L2/trade facts, durable spool/landing, Parquet commit markers, an active-part index and bounded DuckDB compaction to replay/research.

Operate six common perpetual trade lanes for BTC/ETH across Binance, OKX and Bybit, plus primary-venue L2 capture, Deribit option-state feeds, and Hyperliquid funding, open-interest, premium and mark/oracle state.

One live FOMC capture completed 12/12 lanes with 653,722 L2 updates and 4,339,527 trades; v4.4 records zero sequence mismatches, normalization rejections, duplicates or source-identity conflicts, with peak RSS of 2.887 GiB. These are results from that capture.
Used the event data to quantify approximately 68% contraction in displayed BTC/ETH depth and measure subsequent liquidity recovery.

Investigated sequence gaps, reconnect behavior, persistence failures, stale replay boundaries, queue pressure and latency outliers using source evidence, structured logs, replay and reconciliation. Replaced starvation-prone queues with bounded ring-style storage and cooperative draining; propagated integrity failures into research-readiness checks.

Built causal replay using exchange-event, received and available timestamps, immutable landing metadata and bounded research readers to reduce future leakage. Developed a downstream Liquidation Pressure layer retaining provenance, sparse-state semantics, explicit missingness and causal query boundaries without changing authoritative raw facts.

Maintained acceptance criteria, blocker tracking, durability/recovery checks, protected interfaces, closure reports and regression suites across runtime, workstation, replay, dashboard and research components. Stack: Python, TypeScript/Node.js, Rust components, WebSockets, Parquet, DuckDB, local dashboards and structured logging.
bullets: Built multi-exchange market data collection, storage, validation and replay with Python, TypeScript, Parquet and DuckDB.
One documented FOMC capture: 12/12 lanes, 653,722 L2 updates and 4,339,527 trades; observed approximately 68% displayed BTC/ETH depth contraction.

projects.name: Situation Monitor / Market Context Engine
fullBullets: Built a market-context system combining macroeconomic data, economic expectations, news narratives, regulatory/policy information, geopolitical developments and market data for structured event interpretation and research.

The v4.4 historical snapshot reports 106K+ news records and 207K+ structured LLM-extraction rows, with controls for source coverage, missing values, duplicates, schema consistency, reproducibility and downstream research use. These are source-version totals, not current throughput claims.

Developed a Trusted Context Foundation with strict macro identities, immutable pre-event expectations, canonical actual/revision handling, deterministic fact selection, temporal guards and as-of event inspection.

Connected the runtime to Cloudflare Workers/D1 and validated durable write/read/redeploy persistence. The v4.4 snapshot records 5 tables, 11 indexes, 12 triggers and a passing 110-item live parity suite covering ordering, revisions, inspection and temporal guards.

Maintained a production-facing Svelte/SvelteKit/TypeScript frontend, server-side provider access, caching and secret isolation. Kept rule-based narrative/impact signals separate from source facts without unsupported predictive claims; used the system for provenance, normalization, deterministic selection, failure handling, deployment and validation.
bullets: Built a dashboard organizing financial news, economic events and market context with source-linked records, historical selection and Cloudflare Workers/D1 persistence.

projects.name: Quantitative Portfolio Optimization
fullBullets: Built and compared Markowitz, maximum-Sharpe/minimum-volatility, risk-parity, Black-Litterman, CVaR, factor-aware, dynamic/regime-aware and multi-objective portfolio-allocation approaches.

Evaluated changing volatility, correlation, covariance, downside-risk, transaction-cost and market-state assumptions using scenario analysis, Monte Carlo-style testing, drawdown sensitivity and risk-adjusted metrics. Compared assumptions and failure modes rather than treating optimization output as a stand-alone investment decision.
bullets: Compared Markowitz, Black-Litterman, Risk Parity and CVaR methods using Monte Carlo-style tests, scenario analysis and sensitivity to risk and transaction-cost assumptions.

projects.name: Historical Live Perpetual Futures Execution
bullets: Previously ran own-capital USDT-margined perpetual-futures exposure, primarily on OKX. Live trading is paused while the next-generation research and market-data infrastructure is rebuilt and validated.

Monitored order placement/fills, leverage, funding exposure, transaction costs, slippage, position risk and drawdown controls. Compared cross-venue funding, spot-perpetual basis, liquidity/depth, open interest, order flow and liquidations to distinguish venue dislocations from broader market changes.
Kept live, paper/replay and test workflows separate to validate execution and strategy changes before broader use; signals were not treated as automatic execution triggers.

projects.name: Credit Risk Modeling
bullets: Analyzed 34,000+ applicant records using logistic regression, random forest and XGBoost. Evaluated accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, confusion matrices and SHAP-based feature interpretation.
Compared default-risk identification approaches with an emphasis on validation and interpretability; model scores were not treated as stand-alone credit decisions.

projects.name: Legacy API-Based Trading & Monitoring Workflows
bullets: Integrated public REST/WebSocket market-data feeds, local SQLite storage, alert/command workflows, transaction-cost assumptions, position limits, drawdown controls and structured runtime logs.

Used monitoring and validation to identify data-quality issues, execution-assumption gaps, anomalies and recovery needs; documented fixes and follow-up tests. These workflows informed Microstructure Discovery Factory and are no longer the canonical research infrastructure.
